keyFacts: US gallon = 3.78541 L; UK (imperial) gallon = 4.54609 L - so US and UK MPG are different numbers.
Conversion constants: 235.214583 ÷ MPG(US) = L/100km; 282.480936 ÷ MPG(UK) = L/100km.
L/100km and km/L are reciprocals: km/L = 100 ÷ L/100km.
Europe, India and most of Asia use L/100km or km/L; the US uses MPG.
India officially rates cars in km/L (ARAI mileage figures).
Real-world mileage is typically 15-30% worse than lab figures because of traffic, AC and driving style.

fuel-economy-converter.formula:
Via L/100km as the base:
To base: L/100km = 235.214583 ÷ MPG(US); = 282.480936 ÷ MPG(UK); = 100 ÷ km/L.
From base: MPG(US) = 235.214583 ÷ L/100km; km/L = 100 ÷ L/100km.
Example: 30 MPG(US) → 235.214583 ÷ 30 = 7.840 L/100km.

faqs.q: How do I convert MPG to L/100km?
faqs.a: For US MPG: divide 235.21 by the MPG. 30 MPG (US) = 235.21 ÷ 30 = 7.84 L/100km. For UK MPG use 282.48 instead, because the imperial gallon is larger.

faqs.q: What is the difference between US MPG and UK MPG?
faqs.a: The gallon differs: US = 3.785 L, UK imperial = 4.546 L. So 30 MPG (UK) equals only 25 MPG (US) - the same car, two numbers. Always check which gallon a figure uses.

faqs.q: Is higher L/100km better or worse?
faqs.a: Worse. L/100km measures consumption (fuel used), so lower is better. MPG measures economy (distance per fuel), so higher is better. They move in opposite directions.

faqs.q: How do I convert km/L to L/100km?
faqs.a: Divide 100 by the km/L figure. 20 km/L = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 L/100km. They are exact reciprocals.

faqs.q: What is good fuel economy for a car?
faqs.a: Roughly: petrol hatchbacks 15-20 km/L (5-6.7 L/100km) are good; 25+ km/L is excellent (usually hybrids). SUVs at 10-12 km/L are typical for their size.

faqs.q: Why is real mileage lower than the claimed figure?
faqs.a: Claimed figures come from lab test cycles with gentle acceleration and no AC. Real traffic, idling, AC use, tyre pressure and driving style typically cut 15-30% off the claim.
